register.name: Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
register.detail: Launched December 2025 · 4.3 million people targeted · $1.04 billion prioritised
register.note: 9.9 million people in need
register.text: The plan of the Humanitarian Country Team for 2026, prioritising lifesaving and time-critical assistance in the counties where needs are most acute. It was launched at $1.5 billion; the overall requirement is now $1.46 billion.

register.name: Enhancing Climate Resilience in Flood-Prone Areas in Northwestern South Sudan (ECRF)
register.detail: Approved 30 October 2025 by the GCF Board (B.43) · funded activity agreement effective 2 December 2025 · grant
register.note: GCF grant of $44.68 million and $5.32 million co-financing
register.text: Builds climate resilience for about 1.7 million people in flood- and drought-prone north-western South Sudan, including refugees, internally displaced people, returnees and host communities. The World Food Programme is the accredited entity.

register.name: Staff-Monitored Program
register.detail: Staff-level agreement 20 June 2025 · nine months, expected to start in August 2025, pending approval by IMF Management
register.note: Debt forecast at about 58% of GDP in 2024/2025
register.text: Staff-Monitored Programs are informal arrangements between national authorities and IMF staff, without endorsement by the IMF Executive Board. This one supports reforms to strengthen economic resilience to shocks, and follows the conclusion of South Sudan’s Staff Monitored Program with Board Involvement on 15 November 2024.

register.name: Building Institutional Foundations for an Effective Public Service Project
register.detail: Approved, announced 5 September 2024 · IDA grant · three years
register.note: Project total $18 million with $3 million from the Government
register.text: Strengthens the policies, procedures and systems that manage South Sudan’s civil service, over three years. The Government recognises the central role public servants play in delivering services to citizens.

register.name: Resilient Agricultural Livelihoods Project, additional financing
register.detail: Reported 22 December 2023 · financing agreement signed 5 February 2024 · IDA grant of SDR 22.9 million
register.note: Farmers and their organisations, after four years of floods
register.text: Additional IDA financing to strengthen farmers and their organisations and raise agricultural production, with part for livestock and fisheries. The project has provided seeds, other inputs and technology to 52,224 farming households facing acute food insecurity.

register.name: Health Sector Transformation Project
register.detail: Approved 20 December 2023 · IDA grant of SDR 89.1 million (US$117 million equivalent)
register.note: IDA share of a $369.5 million total cost at appraisal
register.text: Expands access to a basic package of health and nutrition services and strengthens the health system, covering 1,158 health facilities in phases. At appraisal, IDA gave $117 million, donor trust funds were to give $242.5 million (expected donors: Canada, the EU, the UK, Gavi, the Global Fund, Sweden and USAID) and the Government $10 million.

register.name: Building Skills for Human Capital Development
register.detail: Financing agreement signed 10 July 2023 · IDA grant · closing date 30 June 2028
register.note: Alongside a grant from the Global Partnership for Education
register.text: Increases skills development opportunities in teaching and digital agriculture, and strengthens capacity to manage the education system.

register.name: Energy Sector Access and Institutional Strengthening Project
register.detail: Approved 25 April 2023 · IDA, Grant E166 · closing date 30 April 2028
register.note: Plus $3 million from Japan’s PHRD fund, $53 million in all
register.text: Grid densification and extension in Juba, a hybrid mini-grid in Yei, and standalone solar systems for health and selected public institutions.
by: Japan Policy and Human Resource Development Fund

register.name: Productive Safety Net for Socioeconomic Opportunities Project
register.detail: Approved, announced 7 June 2022 · IDA grant, including $25 million from the Window for Host Communities and Refugees and $30 million from the Crisis Response Window
register.note: 15 of the 79 counties
register.text: Cash transfers and income-generating opportunities for the most vulnerable households, with investment in child nutrition and development and capacity for several key ministries.

register.name: Women’s Social and Economic Empowerment Project
register.detail: Approved, announced 26 May 2022 · IDA grant
register.note: 91,000 women and 5,200 adolescent girls
register.text: Grants, training and technical assistance for women entrepreneurs to formalise and grow their businesses, and access to vital services for survivors of gender-based violence. It is expected to reach 673,400 people indirectly.

register.name: COVID-19 Emergency Response and Health Systems Preparedness, Additional Financing
register.detail: Approved 31 March 2022 · IDA grant
register.note: COVID-19 vaccines for 30 percent of the population
register.text: Vaccines and health services, with expanded care in Upper Nile, Jonglei, the Greater Pibor Administrative Area and Ruweng, and for refugees, host communities and people hit by floods. It also strengthens disease surveillance, laboratories and emergency preparedness.

register.name: Enhancing Community Resilience and Local Governance Project, Phase II
register.detail: Approved 15 March 2022 · IDA grant
register.note: 920,000 people in 12 of 79 counties
register.text: Improves access to basic infrastructure, strengthens community institutions and enhances flood resilience, widening access to electricity, clean water, health care and education.

register.name: Climate Proof Water4Food Project
register.detail: Approved 15 July 2026 · African Development Fund grant, shared with Ethiopia
register.note: Unity State and Ethiopia’s Gambella region
register.text: Solar-powered water supply, flood management, sanitation in schools and climate-smart farming. Across both countries it targets nearly 80,000 people for safe drinking water and more than 100,000 farmers for training.

register.name: South Sudan Climate Resilient Sanitation and Institutional Support Project
register.detail: Approved 20 November 2024 · addendum approved 8 December 2025 · Transition Support Facility grant
register.note: Faecal sludge treatment for Juba
register.text: Expands and upgrades faecal sludge treatment in Juba, builds sanitation facilities and strengthens waste management, with training and equipment for public sanitation agencies. Dense neighbourhoods such as Munuki and Kator are expected to benefit.

register.name: South Sudan–Uganda Power Interconnection Project
register.detail: Approved 13 December 2024 · $32.50 million African Development Fund grant and €48.93 million EU grant to South Sudan · total project cost $260 million
register.note: Plus a €48.93 million EU grant to South Sudan
register.text: A 299 km power line from Olwiyo in Uganda to Gumbo near Juba, 149 km of it in South Sudan, with two new substations and 1,000 last-mile connections. It is designed to link South Sudan to the East African Power Pool.

register.name: Climate Resilient Agri-Food System Transformation Programme, first phase
register.detail: Approved, announced 12 July 2024 · grant
register.note: Six years, September 2024 to December 2030
register.text: Climate-smart technologies, value chains led by women and young people, digital agricultural and climate advisory services and skills training for about 567,155 direct beneficiaries in nine counties of four states. It targets about 350,000 tonnes of cereals and 179,200 direct jobs.

register.name: Non-Oil Revenue Mobilization and Accountability Project (NORMA II)
register.detail: Approved, announced 12 June 2024 · $6.62 million African Development Fund grant and $1.98 million Transition Support Facility
register.note: Tax revenue beyond oil
register.text: Builds the capacity of South Sudan’s National Revenue Authority, with IT systems for revenue administration and tax collection, tax compliance, audits and training. It also explores new tax bases: value-added, hotel and property taxes.

register.name: UK funding for anticipatory flood action through FAO and WFP
register.detail: WFP release, 30 October 2026 · Jonglei, Unity and Upper Nile
register.note: US$2.8 million
register.text: Early warning, anticipatory cash, livelihood protection, labour-intensive public works and prepositioned supplies, protecting food security and livelihoods before floods become humanitarian emergencies.

register.name: U.S.–South Sudan health cooperation Memorandum of Understanding
register.detail: Signed 25 June 2026 · three years
register.note: U.S. more than $146 million; South Sudan nearly $20 million
register.text: The United States intends to provide more than $146 million to prevent the spread of infectious diseases, including HIV/AIDS. The Government commits nearly $20 million of public revenue to health systems, including clinical care.

register.name: Finnfund and CREI
register.detail: Follow-on investment announced 19 February 2026 · backed by EFSD+
register.note: Finnfund’s total investment in CREI now $10 million
register.text: Finances solar-hybrid power for MTN South Sudan’s 499 telecom sites under a 10-year energy-as-a-service contract. 490 sites have been modernised, reaching over 4 million customers, with a 43% cut in carbon emissions.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Oil
items.label: Of fiscal revenue, IMF, 2024
items.text: A pipeline across Sudan carries 70% of output. Damaged in February 2024, it carries oil again: output reached 157,000 barrels a day early in 2025/26.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Four in five live in the countryside.

items.name: Water for South Sudan
items.text: Has drilled more than 640 wells in remote villages since 2005, providing water to more than 500,000 people, mainly in rural villages of the Bahr el Ghazal region. Its employees are all South Sudanese.

items.name: Ezra Construction and Development Group
items.text: Developed and financed in-house a 20 MW solar power plant with battery storage, which supplies bulk energy to the Juba Electricity Distribution Company. The plant can supply electricity to up to 16,000 households in Juba.

items.name: Loreto Rumbek
items.text: Runs a girls’ secondary school opened in 2008, a primary school and a primary health care centre in Maker Kuei, Rumbek. Around 400 girls attend the secondary school and 1,200 children the primary school.
